findings.title: Embedded post meta link light-theme color flipped from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The PR is meant to change only the $secondary-based branch, but here the primary-based (light theme) value was changed from 30% to 70% and the two values were swapped. In the light theme the bold link text becomes a 70%-lightness gray on a white background, which is close to unreadable. The conversion should keep the first argument at 30% and use 70% for $secondary.

findings.title: Custom message length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: The original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value is now 30% lightness, far darker than before, and the dark-theme value is 70%, so both sides are swapped. The desktop equivalent in desktop/modal.scss (`.custom-message-length`) uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))`, so the mobile and desktop modals now render this text differently in the light theme. The first argument should stay at 70% and the second should be 30%.

findings.title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme name text becomes noticeably lighter. The dark-theme branch is also not the mirror of 30% (which would be 70% for $secondary). The 50/50 values look copied from the sibling `.title` rule directly below, which was originally 50%. Every other hunk in this PR keeps the original value as the first argument, so this one breaks the pattern. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme name color to a lighter gray, which the PR's stated goal (dark themes only) does not call for. The same selector in desktop/user.scss was changed the same way, so the bug is duplicated. The intended conversion is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic map heading light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme heading becomes much lighter than before. The desktop rule for the same `.topic-map h3` selector in desktop/topic-post.scss uses the mirrored pair 20%/80%, so the mobile and desktop headings now diverge. The correct value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Comment still describes the topic-list default color as a plain scale-color
findings.body: The comment says the default table cell color in the topic list is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. After this PR that default is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%))`, and the coldmap rules below it use that form. The comment is now misleading for anyone maintaining these colors.

findings.title: Category badge-notification color left unconverted in a file this PR otherwise converts
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses plain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. The rest of this file (lines 48, 51, 55, 69, 246, 301) was converted to the theme-aware form. In dark themes this element keeps the primary-derived color the PR is meant to replace, so the conversion is incomplete.

findings.title: Uploading indicator uses scale-color on $secondary with no theme branch
findings.body: `#file-uploading` uses `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)`. In the light theme $secondary is white, and scale-color cannot lighten white, so the text stays white on the light composer background (`dark-light-diff(...)`). This is the same family of color rule the PR converts, and it sits in a file the PR touches, but it was left unconverted. It should use dark-light-choose with a primary-based light-theme value.
